REASONING:
Step 1 – Frame the project  
- Objective: “increase the capacity and reliability of the transmission grid in the Project Areas for renewable energy integration.” (PDO statement)  
- Scope: Construction of a 220 kV double‑circuit Baganuur‑Choir transmission line and expansion of associated substations (Component 1, US$45.84 M) plus capacity‑building and implementation support (Component 2, US$1.16 M IBRD + US$0.84 M counterpart).  
- Delivery model: IBRD loan US$47 M, implementing agency Ministry of Energy (MOE) with a Project Steering Committee (PSC) and a Project Management Office (PMO); Owner’s Engineer to support procurement and supervision.  
- Timeline: Expected approval 21‑Nov‑2024, closing 31‑Dec‑2029, implementation to start 2025, major construction to be finished before the winter season each year.  
- Budget: Total operation cost US$47.84 M (IBRD US$47 M, counterpart US$0.84 M).  
- Key stakeholders: Borrower (Mongolia), MOE, Ministry of Finance (MOF), National Power Transmission Grid (NPTG), World Bank, local contractors, private renewable developers, local communities, women workforce.  
- External dependencies: Availability of qualified local contractors and imported construction materials, right‑of‑way acquisition, regulatory approvals from the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC), climate‑hazard exposure (floods, landslides, extreme cold).

Step 2 – Category sweep (candidate risks with supporting text)  
Technical: winter‑season construction deadline; unqualified construction materials; bird‑collision and biodiversity issues; climate‑hazard exposure.  
Financial: sector electricity price below cost, projected 36 % deficit; budgeting/mis‑allocation risk; CAPEX overruns; FM risk from inexperienced PMO staff; counterpart‑funding delivery.  
Schedule: winter‑season delay; election‑cycle changes; procurement evaluation language gap; coordination delays.  
Stakeholder: community safety & access restrictions; gender gap; grievance handling; corruption perception.  
Political/Regulatory: change of government officials; regulator blocking additional VRE connections.  
Environmental: bird collisions, EMF, noise, soil erosion, wetland disturbance; climate‑hazard risks.  
Organizational: PMO not yet established, weak internal controls, lack of English‑proficient evaluators, OHS risks.  
External: 75‑80 % of construction materials imported, pandemic/border‑closure risk; limited local supplier capacity.

Step 3 – Evidence filter  
All listed risks are directly quoted in the PAD (see evidence statements below). No risk without textual support was kept.

Step 4 – Assess & mitigate  
Likelihood (1‑5) and Impact (1‑5) assigned with brief justification; concrete mitigation actions drafted.

Step 5 – Consolidate  
Duplicates merged; 20 distinct risks retained.
